cases.notes: Whole raw request body deserialized polymorphically by Jackson default-typing, with the concrete runtime type resolved from an attacker-controlled type hint embedded in the JSON itself (CWE-502) -- modeled on Netflix's real playback-resume mutation resolver (docs/research/site-architecture-survey-functionality-netflix.md). No single named field carries the taint (the entire body is the sink input), so `param` is the literal string "body" rather than a form/query field name -- a deliberate, explicitly-recorded convention for this whole-body-JSON shape (CC-LAB-0174), distinct from every other `param` value in this project's ground truth, all of which name a real field/header/query key. `LABGEN-JV-0001` in lab/manifests/insecure_deserialization_spring_boot_sample.yaml, CC-LAB-0173/FR-LAB-79 (Netflix cell ported into the shared `spring_boot` package) -- never a PFF-* case.

Whole raw request body (an XML partner content-metadata feed) parsed with a default-configured DocumentBuilderFactory that resolves external entities/DOCTYPE declarations (CWE-611) -- modeled on Netflix's real B2B content-metadata ingestion surface (DDEX ERN messages are XSD-validated XML; Netflix is a confirmed EIDR participant alongside the major studios and MovieLabs -- see lab/manifests/xxe_netflix_sample.yaml's own sourcing note for the fact-vs-inference split). No single named field carries the taint, so `param` is the literal string "body", same whole-body convention as NFLX-0001 (CC-LAB-0174). `rendering` is "server" (plain text, not JSON) -- distinct from NFLX-0001's "server-json". `LABGEN-JV-0003` in lab/manifests/xxe_netflix_sample.yaml, CC-LAB-0179 (reuses TrackerNest's own already-built xml_external_entities_enabled/_disabled shape, CC-LAB-0131, at a new Netflix-specific route) -- never a PFF-* case.

Whole raw request body deserialized polymorphically by Jackson default-typing, with the concrete runtime type resolved from an attacker-controlled type hint embedded in the JSON itself (CWE-502) -- the identical mechanism NFLX-0001 already models (source jackson_body, sinks jackson_default_typing_deserialize/jackson_typed_allowlist_deserialize, both via _SOURCE_OVERRIDE_BY_OP, CC-LAB-0173), reused verbatim at a second, distinct real Netflix feature: switching the account's active profile (a real, core Netflix feature -- Netflix's own Help Center documents up to 5 profiles per account, each with its own maturity-rating/autoplay/subtitle preferences), not a cosmetic rename of NFLX-0001's own playback-resume mutation. No single named field carries the taint, so `param` is the literal string "body", same whole-body convention as NFLX-0001/NFLX-0002 (CC-LAB-0174). `LABGEN-JV-0005` in lab/manifests/insecure_deserialization_netflix_profiles_sample.yaml, CC-LAB-0184/FR-LAB-124 (Netflix's third real page, zero new generator code) -- never a PFF-* case.

An account_id query param used to look up account billing details (payment method, last invoice amount, billing cycle) with no check that it matches the caller's own X-Account-Id (CWE-639/862, broken object-level authorization / IDOR) -- modeled on a real, plausible Netflix account-billing/payment-method page, a textbook OWASP API1:2023 BOLA surface, and Netflix's first access_control/IDOR page (the Twitch/go_net_http pick already has this mechanism, TWCH-0003/TWCH-0007, but Netflix never did before this entry). Reuses lab/safety_matrix.yaml's existing db_row_by_id_lookup sink family and no_ownership_check/identity_match_before_fetch ops (added by CC-LAB-0063) -- no new safety-matrix entry needed; this is, however, this mechanism's first instantiation for the spring_boot stack (a new source module and two new sink modules, since this stack's shape has no separate transform stage -- see fuzzlab/labgen/emitters/spring_boot/modules.py's own docstring). `X-Account-Id` is a fixed demo header standing in for the caller's own authenticated identity (this stack has no session/auth system yet; the header models only the ownership-check-bypass mechanism in isolation, never a real session/auth system, the same declared simplification CC-LAB-0178 already used for go_net_http's own X-Broadcaster-Id header). `LABGEN-JV-0007` in lab/manifests/access_control_netflix_billing_sample.yaml, CC-LAB-0187/FR-LAB-127 -- never a PFF-* case. Verified live: AccessControlIdorStrategy (already built for TWCH-0003/CC-FUZZ-0029, keyed on vuln_class=access_control + sink shape, not per-stack) confirms this new vulnerable twin with zero new detection code, and correctly does not confirm the secure twin (LABGEN-JV-0008) -- the first proof this strategy generalizes across stacks (go_net_http -> spring_boot), not just across routes on the same stack.

A subscription plan-upgrade/downgrade endpoint (switching between Basic/Standard/Premium tiers, a real, plausible, core Netflix streaming-subscription feature) that trusts a client-supplied monthly_charge field and reflects it verbatim as the new plan's charge, instead of recomputing the real price server-side from the requested plan_tier (CWE-807, price_integrity_bypass). Reuses lab/safety_matrix.yaml's existing payment_charge_amount sink family and client_trusted_amount/server_recomputed_amount ops (added by CC-LAB-0063) -- no new safety-matrix entry needed; the only prior real implementation of this concern project-wide is php_laravel's Booking.com checkout charge (CC-LAB-0212), so this is this concern's first instantiation on spring_boot, and Netflix's first price_integrity_bypass page. Unlike php_laravel's source+transform+sink triad, this stack's shape has no separate transform stage (see fuzzlab/labgen/emitters/spring_boot/modules.py's own docstring), so the op selects the sink directly (this stack's existing ssti/xxe/access_control convention): the vulnerable twin (client_trusted_amount) reflects whatever monthly_charge the client sends; the secure twin (server_recomputed_amount) discards it entirely and looks the real charge up in a fixed, server-owned plan-tier-to-price map keyed only by the non-numeric plan_tier field, failing closed (HTTP 400) on an unrecognized tier rather than silently defaulting. `sink_context` widened additively to "payment_charge" (fuzzlab/labels/schemas/labels.schema.json) -- checked first, no existing enum value describes a price/charge amount reflected in a JSON response (Booking.com's own BKNG-0003 used "sql" because its sink was a real DB insert; this sink has no DB write at all). `param` is the literal string "body" (CC-LAB-0188's own original entry instead used the per-field name "monthly_charge", modeled on NFLX-0004's own query-param convention -- corrected here, during CC-FUZZ-0037's own real end-to-end pipeline verification, to this project's actual whole-body-JSON convention: fuzzlab.harness.auto.points_from_ground_truth only sets a body point's Content-Type to application/json when param=="body" exactly, the same gate CC-LAB-0182's own mass_assignment ground truth had to satisfy; the price-integrity oracle strategy builds its own JSON probe bodies from hardcoded field names regardless of param, so this correction changes nothing about what is sent, only whether the harness recognizes the point as JSON at all), the same whole-body convention NFLX-0001/0002/0003 use, since PriceIntegrityBypassStrategy needs a JSON body point to send its own probes at all -- not because more than one field carries the taint (the account_id-style single-named-query-param convention was simply the wrong analogy for a `location="body"` point, which is gated differently). `LABGEN-JV-0009`/`0010` in lab/manifests/price_integrity_netflix_subscription_sample.yaml, CC-LAB-0188/FR-LAB-128 -- never a PFF-* case. Verified live (real mvn build/boot/HTTP round trip): a manipulated `{"plan_tier":"standard","monthly_charge":0.01}` request is trusted and reflected verbatim by the vulnerable twin, while the secure twin ignores it and returns the real Standard price ($15.49); a second plan_tier (basic/premium) proves the secure twin's lookup is genuinely data-driven, not a disguised constant (the same proof style CC-LAB-0212's own room_type=deluxe case established). Detection: `PriceIntegrityBypassStrategy`/`R-PRICE-INTEGRITY` (CC-FUZZ-0037/CC-AUD-0025) confirms the vulnerable twin and correctly fails closed on the secure twin, verified live against a real booted instance.

A per-profile avatar-image upload endpoint (a real, plausible Netflix feature -- each of a Netflix account's up-to-five profiles has its own avatar image) that trusts the caller-supplied filename and multipart Content-Type: the uploaded bytes are written verbatim under the caller's own filename into a web-served directory, and served back with a Content-Type derived from that same filename's extension via Spring's own MediaTypeFactory (falling back to the caller's own multipart Content-Type header) rather than the file's real bytes (CWE-434) -- the same well-documented CWE-434-to-XSS chain CC-LAB-0186's own go_net_http/Twitch emote-upload page models (Java, like Go, has no PHP-style 'the web server executes an uploaded script' footgun), so an uploaded .html/.svg file is served back same-origin as text/html/image/svg+xml, letting an embedded <script> execute (stored XSS via unrestricted file upload). This is lab/safety_matrix.yaml's existing fs_web_root_write sink family / unrestricted_file_upload concern's FIRST instantiation for the spring_boot stack (a new source module, ReadUploadedAvatarFileSource, reading the upload off the raw Servlet 3.1+ Part API since every complexity template's handler signature takes only HttpServletRequest, and two new sink modules reusing CC-LAB-0063's existing no_extension_check/extension_allowlist_mime_check op names verbatim -- no new safety-matrix entry needed) -- confirmed absent by grep before starting. The secure twin (extension_allowlist_mime_check) allowlists exactly .png/.jpg/.jpeg (narrower than go_net_http's own allowlist, which also accepts .gif/.webp -- a deliberate, stated scoping to the two formats this sink's own minimal magic-byte check can actually sniff) AND requires the uploaded bytes' own magic-byte signature to match a real PNG or JPEG -- a documented design choice over Files.probeContentType, which is platform/OS-dependent and not a deterministic real-bytes sniff (see ExtensionAllowlistMagicByteCheckSink's own docstring); writes under a fully server-chosen filename and always serves the SNIFFED content type. `param`/`location` are `file`/`body` (the real multipart field name), the same deliberate convention CC-LAB-0186's own TWCH-0009 ground truth already established -- not the `body`/`body` whole-body-point convention this directory's other, whole-JSON-body cases use, since `file` genuinely is this shape's one tainted field and `body` would incorrectly trigger points_from_ground_truth's JSON-content-type auto-detection. `rendering` is `server` (the response body on success is the raw uploaded bytes with a dynamic Content-Type, never JSON), matching TWCH-0009's own departure from this directory's usual `server-json`/`server` split. `LABGEN-JV-0011`/`0012` in lab/manifests/unrestricted_file_upload_netflix_avatar_sample.yaml, CC-LAB-0191/FR-LAB-131 -- never a PFF-* case. Detection: `UnrestrictedFileUploadContentTypeTrustStrategy` (already built for TWCH-0009/CC-FUZZ-0036/CC-AUD-0023) confirms this new vulnerable twin with zero new detection code, and correctly does not confirm the secure twin -- the strategy's own real, executed multipart two-probe differential over a live-booted spring_boot app confirms this generalizes across stacks (go_net_http -> spring_boot) exactly the way it reads the served Content-Type off the same POST response for either stack, verified live, not assumed from the strategy's own generic-looking code alone.

An account-settings-update endpoint (a real, plausible Netflix feature -- updating a display name/bio) that parses the raw request body with a plain Jackson 3 JsonMapper.readTree() and assigns EVERY field present onto the account record's in-memory representation, including `is_partner` -- never exposed by this endpoint's own intended form (CWE-915, mass assignment). This is lab/safety_matrix.yaml's existing orm_entity_bulk_assign sink family / mass_assignment concern's FIRST instantiation for the spring_boot stack, reusing its existing unfiltered_object_assign/typed_schema_allowlist ops verbatim (CC-LAB-0063, already instantiated on php_current/ruby_rails/php_laravel/go_net_http -- see CC-LAB-0182's own go_net_http/Twitch channel-profile page for the equivalent minimal pair) -- no new safety-matrix entry needed. Java has no ORM/ActiveRecord bulk-assign call to misuse either, so this mirrors go_net_http's own idiomatic modeling: the vulnerable sink reads the whole JSON tree itself and assigns whatever keys are present; the secure sink reads the identical body but only ever pulls display_name/bio out of it, leaving is_partner at its seeded value regardless of what the request carries. `param`/`location` are the whole-body-point convention (`body`/`body`) this directory already uses for other no-per-field-param whole-body cases (e.g. NFLX-0001/NFLX-0003), since is_partner is one of several JSON keys in the request body, not a single named param -- also required for fuzzlab.harness.auto.points_from_ground_truth's own content-type detection, which only marks a body point as JSON when param=="body" exactly. `LABGEN-JV-0013`/`0014` in lab/manifests/mass_assignment_netflix_settings_sample.yaml, CC-LAB-0192/FR-LAB-132 -- never a PFF-* case. Detection: both twins deliberately echo the resulting record as `{"display_name":...,"bio":...,"is_partner":...}` -- the exact JSON shape MassAssignmentPrivilegedFieldStrategy (fuzzlab/oracle/strategies.py, built for Twitch's TWCH-0006/CC-AUD-0022/CC-FUZZ-0035) already hardcodes (field name is_partner, intended fields display_name/bio) -- this session's own 'fixed demo field name as declared simplification' convention, verified live to need zero new detection code, the first proof this strategy generalizes across stacks (go_net_http -> spring_boot).

A Bearer JWT's own alg:none header is honored, skipping signature verification entirely and trusting the token's own forged claims (CWE-347, the real auth0/node-jsonwebtoken GHSA-8cf7-32gw-wr33 bug -- docs/research/corpus-examples/auth-session/node/vulnerable-1.js) -- modeled on an account-level viewing-preferences lookup (maturity rating, autoplay, subtitle language), a realistic Bearer-JWT-protected API-edge shape for this app identity, distinct from every one of this app's other 7 real pages (none of which use header-carried auth). Reuses lab/safety_matrix.yaml's existing jwt_signature_verification sink family and jwt_alg_none_default/jwt_none_alg_opt_in ops (added by CC-LAB-0063; already instantiated on go_net_http, CC-LAB-0180) -- no new safety-matrix entry needed; this is spring_boot's first instantiation of this mechanism. A hand-rolled JWT parser/verifier using only JDK standard-library primitives (java.util.Base64, javax.crypto.Mac, java.security.MessageDigest) -- no third-party JWT dependency, matching go_net_http's own 'hand-rolled parser is the vulnerability' framing rather than a real library's own CVE. The tainted value is carried in the Authorization header, not a query/body field, so `param` is set to the literal header name `Authorization` (the same header-carried-value convention TWCH-0001/TWCH-0004 established, CC-LAB-0174). Response echoes the decoded token's own channel_id/role claims verbatim -- the same 'fixed demo field name as declared simplification' convention CC-LAB-0182/CC-LAB-0192's own mass_assignment ground truth already establish, letting JwtAlgNoneConfusionStrategy (already built for Twitch's TWCH-0004/CC-FUZZ-0033/CC-AUD-0020) generalize to this new stack with zero new detection code -- verified live in tests/test_labgen_spring_boot_netflix_jwt_preferences_live_boot.py: confirms the vulnerable twin (LABGEN-JV-0015) and correctly does not confirm the secure twin (LABGEN-JV-0016). `LABGEN-JV-0015` in lab/manifests/jwt_alg_confusion_netflix_sample.yaml, served at /api/account/preferences, CC-LAB-0193/FR-LAB-133 -- never a PFF-* case.

A thumbnail_url query parameter is fetched server-side with no scheme or resolved-IP allowlist check (CWE-918) -- modeled on a partner-content thumbnail-import feature (importing a thumbnail image from a partner-supplied URL for newly-ingested partner content), a real, plausible feature given Netflix's own confirmed B2B content-ingestion surface, /api/content/import (CC-LAB-0179), genuinely distinct from that endpoint's own XML-metadata-feed ingestion, not a cosmetic rename of it. Reuses lab/safety_matrix.yaml's existing server_side_http_fetch sink family and unchecked_url_fetch/scheme_and_resolved_ip_allowlist ops (added by CC-LAB-0063; already instantiated TWICE on go_net_http -- CC-LAB-0172's /api/clips/thumbnail and CC-LAB-0185's /clips/download) -- no new safety-matrix entry needed; this is spring_boot's first instantiation of this mechanism. Reuses the pre-existing query_param source verbatim (already used by ssti/spel_injection) -- the same query-param-carried-URL contract go_net_http's own read_url_query_param source established, letting a generic Candidate(location="query") probe drive this shape identically to go_net_http's own SSRF cells. Both sinks are ported idiomatically from go_net_http's own UncheckedUrlFetchSink/SchemeAndResolvedIpAllowlistSink (CC-LAB-0172) to java.net.http.HttpClient, with java.net.InetAddress.getAllByName doing real DNS resolution before the fetch (the JDK's own net.LookupIP-then-validate analog), checked against the RESOLVED address actually dialed, not just the hostname string. The vulnerable twin's response body is the fetched resource's own body verbatim, matching go_net_http's own io.Copy(w, resp.Body) shape -- exactly what SsrfInBandMarkerStrategy's own confirm() (fuzzlab/oracle/strategies.py, already built for Twitch's go_net_http cells) checks for, letting that existing strategy (and its SsrfOobStrategy fallback) generalize to this new stack with zero new detection code AND zero new sender/candidate plumbing -- verified live in tests/test_labgen_spring_boot_netflix_thumbnail_ssrf_live_boot.py: confirms the vulnerable twin (LABGEN-JV-0017) and correctly does not confirm the secure twin (LABGEN-JV-0018). `LABGEN-JV-0017` in lab/manifests/ssrf_netflix_thumbnail_sample.yaml, served at /api/content/thumbnail-import, CC-LAB-0194/FR-LAB-134 -- never a PFF-* case.
